synthesis.trait: Confronts and demands answers from police authority figures about his missing daughter, even when restrained or told to stop
Capacity for sudden physical violence against a police officer when overwhelmed by frustration and mistaken identity
Emotional vulnerability surfaces -- his voice trails off and he nearly breaks -- when recounting the loss of his daughter

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Capacity for sudden physical violence against a police officer when overwhelmed by frustration and mistaken identity
turning_points.what_changes: Pete's demand for information escalates from shouting at officers who restrain him (scene121_beat2) to actually decking a cop hard enough to require an ice pack, a genuine breaking point never previously reached, revealing a limit to his composure rather than just a louder version of his demanding behavior.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Confronts and demands answers from police authority figures about his missing daughter, even when restrained or told to stop
turning_points.what_changes: Pete's earlier complaint that 'Nobody returns my calls... You won't even gimmie an update' is directly answered by his later accusation 'I called you guys. I fucking warned ya's. But you didn't listen' -- the same grievance about being ignored, now confirmed and completed rather than merely repeated.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Emotional vulnerability surfaces -- his voice trails off and he nearly breaks -- when recounting the loss of his daughter
turning_points.what_changes: The restrained, trailing-off near-break of scene122_beat5 ('My little girl... That was the last time I ever saw her.') becomes full visible collapse here -- wiping away tears, crying, and directly begging 'Someone tell me where's my baby girl?' -- a more exposed and complete breakdown than the earlier beat's suppressed pause.
